background_notes.fact: In the Fourier completion H^s, diagonal multipliers of modulus one are isometries, deletion of the zero coefficient is a contraction, and Fourier truncations converge. If a Fourier sequence is absolutely summable, its Fourier series converges uniformly to a bounded continuous representative with supremum norm at most its l1 norm. For f in L2, sum_(k!=0)|hat f(k)|/|k| <= (sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||2. Consequently the displayed Dinv bounds also hold for general f after replacing f by Pf. For u in H1 its distributional derivative belongs to L2, has coefficients ik hat u(k), and Dinv(partial_x u)=u-P0u.

grounds.reason: H^s is the weighted Fourier completion and L2=H0.
The S_t multiplier has modulus one.
P deletes exactly the zero Fourier coefficient.
Dinv has the reciprocal derivative multiplier off zero and vanishes at zero.
The inputs are L2 or H1 exactly as required.

background_notes.justification: The norm assertions follow termwise in the squared weighted l2 norm. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the l1 series by the product of the stated l2 norms; sum k^(-2) converges by integral comparison. The tails of an absolutely summable Fourier series uniformly bound the tails of its partial sums. Multiplication of coefficients by ik gives ||partial_x u||2^2=sum k^2|hat u(k)|^2 and ||u||H1^2=||u||2^2+||partial_x u||2^2. The inverse derivative identity follows coefficientwise, so S001's use of the mean and derivative is legitimate.

background_notes.fact: On this normalized torus, for u,v in H1 with the H1-to-L-infinity bound derived in S001, uv belongs to H1, (uv)'=u'v+uv' weakly, and ||uv||H1 <= C||u||H1||v||H1. Also ||wv||2<=||w||2||v||infinity for w in L2 and bounded v.

grounds.reason: S001 first establishes the H1 supremum bound from the mean and inverse derivative estimate.
H1 is the completion of polynomials in the derivative-equivalent norm.

background_notes.justification: For polynomials the product rule and ||uv||2<=||u||infinity||v||2 bound the L2 norm and both derivative terms. Approximate H1 inputs by Fourier polynomials. The proved supremum bound gives uniform convergence, while the same estimates make products and derivative expressions Cauchy in L2. Their limits satisfy the weak derivative formula and the bound. The mixed estimate follows directly by integrating |wv|^2<=||v||infinity^2|w|^2.

background_notes.fact: For u,v in L2, uv is in L1 and hat(uv)(k)=sum_r hat u(r)hat v(k-r), an absolutely convergent series bounded by ||u||2||v||2 for every integer k. Moreover sum_(k!=0)k^2(1+k^2)^(-23/14) and sum_(k!=0)k^(-2) converge.

grounds.reason: u=S_t f and v=S_t g are L2 with unchanged norms; the second product uses u=f,v=g.
The L2 norm is the l2 norm of Fourier coefficients.

background_notes.justification: Cauchy-Schwarz proves both integrability of uv and absolute convergence of the convolution for each k. Polynomial approximants converge in L2, their products converge in L1 by the two-term product difference estimate, and Fourier coefficient evaluation is bounded by the L1 norm. Passing to the limit proves the convolution identity. For |k|>=1 the first weight is at most |k|^(2-23/7)=|k|^(-9/7). Integral comparison proves convergence of this series and of the reciprocal-square series. These are finite values of infinite series, as needed in S002.

background_notes.fact: A bilinear map on dense subspaces with bound ||Q(x,y)||Z<=C||x||X||y||Y, where Z is complete, has a unique bounded bilinear extension to X times Y. The bounds in S001–S002 therefore extend their bounded polynomial products. Mean-zero distributions A0 with Dinv A0 in L2 can be approximated by mean-zero Fourier truncations in the norm ||Dinv A0||2.

grounds.reason: The Sobolev spaces are complete Fourier completions with dense polynomials.
For mean-zero A0 the displayed norm is a weighted l2 coefficient norm and has no zero-mode kernel.
The H1 product and J bounds are proved on polynomials.

background_notes.justification: For approximants x_n,y_n the difference Q(x_n,y_n)-Q(x_m,y_m)=Q(x_n-x_m,y_n)+Q(x_m,y_n-y_m) tends to zero by the bound and boundedness of convergent sequences. Completeness supplies the limit; the same estimate gives independence and uniqueness. Fourier tails tend to zero in the displayed A0 norm. Product limits agree with the actual L1 or L2 products by the corresponding product difference estimates. Thus the extension argument introduces no new product or unsupported limit.

background_notes.fact: For smooth periodic paths on a compact time interval, the spatial Fourier expansions, their time derivatives used in S003, and the products of these series can be differentiated and integrated termwise. On each smooth piece the fundamental theorem of calculus gives the endpoint difference of J; for continuous piecewise smooth paths the one-sided J endpoint values coincide.

grounds.reason: The normal-form argument explicitly restricts to smooth mean-zero paths and then continuous piecewise smooth paths on [a,b].
The time-dependent S multiplier is exp(itk^3), whose time derivative introduces only a polynomial factor in k.
J consists of these multipliers, inverse derivatives, projection and multiplication.

background_notes.justification: Repeated spatial integration by parts bounds Fourier coefficients, including those of the required time derivatives, by arbitrarily high inverse powers of the frequency, uniformly on each compact smooth time piece. Choosing the decay exponent above all polynomial factors gives absolutely and uniformly convergent double series and differentiated series. Uniform convergence justifies their integrals and derivatives. Applying the fundamental theorem to J yields S003's integral identity. Its polynomial formula is continuous in smooth-path values, so adjacent endpoint terms cancel. The zero summands r=0 or s=0 are excluded by Dinv's zero convention; mean-zero inputs ensure that omitting them also loses no B term.
